discovery: Invention and development of the optical lattice atomic clock

nominees.name: Hidetoshi Katori
nominees.affiliation: University of Tokyo and RIKEN, Japan

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / precision measurement
motivation: Katori conceived the optical lattice clock: thousands of neutral atoms trapped at a 'magic' wavelength, where the lattice light shifts both clock levels equally, so they can be interrogated without perturbation. Ye turned the idea into a working measurement method. He built ultrastable lasers, characterised systematics to the 10^-18 level and below, and used many-body and spin-resolved control of strontium clocks. Together they improved timekeeping by about two orders of magnitude beyond the caesium standard. Lattice clocks now resolve the gravitational redshift over millimetre height differences, enable relativistic geodesy, set tight limits on variations of fundamental constants and on ultralight dark matter, and are driving the redefinition of the SI second. This is a new measurement paradigm. It reaches foundational physics and practical application through one conceptually simple idea, carried out with superb experimental craft.
